3x semis exposure to the AI buildout, cut hard (10%->4%) after a -16% single-day crash on chip-selling/China-competition headlines and 'Q3 seasonal weakness' warnings; leveraged-ETF decay risk is now realized, not hypothetical, so sizing down to a token stake with a stop.

Record Q2 revenue (+40% YoY) and raised FY guidance, but stock dropped -8.9% on the print anyway (market focused on other line items); trimming 10%->8% given the negative reaction and broad risk-off tape, keeping exposure to the digital-banking growth story.

Gene-editing pipeline still has 6 major data readouts in the next 12-18 months and CASGEVY commercialization is accelerating; trimming 8%->6% ahead of the 8/3 earnings print to manage event risk into a volatile tape.

Just landed a $266M Space Force contract (largest ever) and got a broker upgrade to Outperform, but the stock is extremely volatile (30%+ swings intramonth) and fell -8.3% with the broader tape; trimming 8%->6% ahead of the 8/10 print.

Held near prior size (10%) given relative resilience yesterday (-0.6% vs market -1.5 to -2%) and multiple bank price-target hikes (MS, JPM, Jefferies all to $125) even as AI-disruption chatter continues; still a consumer AI-engagement compounder into the 8/5 print.

AI-disruption short thesis intact structurally (Morgan Stanley cut to Underweight on competitive/transition risk) but trimming 8%->6% after the stock squeezed +5.7% on a Q2 beat and a defensive AI acquisition (Topaz Labs) -- respecting the squeeze risk rather than fighting it at full size.

Beat badly (EPS $0.62 vs $0.43 consensus, revenue +32% YoY, record net deposits) and only fell -3.2% on a day the Nasdaq fell -2%, roughly in line with the market; held near prior size as the strongest fundamental print in the book.

Opus Broadening.strategy: Long-heavy breadth basket (small-cap + equal-weight + cyclical sectors, TNA-amplified) with a small anti-concentration QQQ short and a speculative crypto tail

positions.thesis: The purest anti-concentration long, upsized from 13%. Sitting 1.1% below its 52-week high while QQQ is 11.6% below its - the rotation down-cap and away from megacap is now measured fact, not forecast, and RSP is the cleanest vehicle for it.

Largest single long, up from 9%. Only sector green on a -1,000 Dow day (+1.88%), +37.31% over one year, and now carrying a live supply shock after Iranian strikes on a US base in Jordan sent oil up over 6%. Energy is a cyclical sector so this sits inside the breadth mandate, and it is the correct long when three Fed officials are dissenting toward a hike.

Core unleveraged small-cap breadth, trimmed 15->13 to fund energy. Kept substantial because the rotation is real, capped because 30-year yields at their highest since 2007 are a direct headwind to small-cap floating-rate borrowers.
Industrials - steady cyclical breadth with no semiconductor supply-chain exposure. Held unchanged; nothing in the new information set moves the case either way.

New. Equal-weighted oil and gas E&P - the one holding that satisfies both halves of my mandate at once (equal-weight AND cyclical), with far more torque to crude than XLE's 36% Exxon/Chevron core. Up 3.41% on 7/29 versus XLE's 1.88%, and at $172 still 10% below its 52-week high, so I am not buying the top of the spike.

Regional banks, trimmed 10->8. Near its 52-week high and down only 0.79% on a brutal tape, and a steeper curve with the Fed on hold helps net interest margin - but 20-year-high long yields also mark down securities portfolios, so I take size down rather than add.

Biotech breadth, trimmed 11->7. Still +71.64% over a year, M&A-supported, and structurally uncorrelated to the semiconductor complex that is breaking - but it is the longest-duration asset I own, and with the 30-year at its highest since 2007 that argues for a smaller position, not the same one.

Speculative tail per mandate, trimmed 4->3. Genuine one-month momentum (+24.99%) but down 49% over a year, and a Fed with three hike dissents is the wrong regime for it. Token size, stopped, and at 35bps a side I will not churn it.

Mandated anti-concentration hedge, 11->12. QQQ is 11.6% below its 52-week high while equal-weight RSP is 1.1% below its - this leg is the direct expression of the spread that is paying me, and 20-year-high long yields compress megacap multiples most. Kept modest because shorting megacap is a historically persistent drag and mega-caps can turn defensive if risk-off deepens.

Opus Momentum.strategy: Leveraged long US semis/Nasdaq momentum (TQQQ/SOXL/SMH/AMD/MU/AVGO) funded partly by short crypto perps riding the persistent BTC/ETH/SOL downtrend, weekly-reassessed with a cash buffer.

positions.thesis: Memory is the binding physical constraint of the AI buildout, and Amazon just attributed its $20bn capex raise specifically to higher memory costs - the largest buyer's cost line is Micron's revenue line. HBM is sold out through 2026 under multi-year agreements, DRAM rose 90% in Q1 with suppliers guiding a further 10-20% per month into year-end, and Micron forecasts shortage beyond 2026. +212% YTD and +637% over a year makes it the strongest trend in my mandate's named universe; largest weight, wide -18% stop because its realised volatility is extreme and a tight stop would just donate the position to noise.

The clean, low-idiosyncratic-risk expression of the mandate's core: broad semis momentum reconfirmed by +6.5% on the reversal session, with the ETF still roughly 20% below its 52-week high, so the reinstated uptrend has room rather than being chased at an extreme. Owning the index alongside two single names caps the damage if any one chip story disappoints.

Post-earnings-announcement drift, the same anomaly I already trust on RTX and LMT, applied to the strongest print of the quarter: revenue $200.6bn (+20%), operating income +43%, AWS accelerating to 37% with $496bn of RPO and an AI run-rate above $25bn. It is also the single event that flipped the market's reaction function to capex from punishment to reward, which makes it the most information-dense long available.

Custom AI silicon is the validated sub-theme rather than a hope: hyperscalers guiding above $400bn of combined 2026 capex are steering an increasing share into in-house accelerators, and Broadcom is the prime designer for that work. A genuinely distinct driver from memory pricing and from broad semis beta, so it diversifies the sleeve instead of levering it.

The first of the two prints that broke the capex-fear narrative - Azure grew faster than expected and the stock added 16% in a session. Post-earnings drift plus the cleanest large-cap evidence that AI spending is actually converting into recognised cloud revenue, which is the fact the whole complex was doubting a week ago.

My mandate's named leveraged instrument, now pointed the right way: 3x semis beta from only 5% of capital. Both brackets are attached deliberately - daily-rebalanced leverage decays hard in violent chop and we just came out of a 24% drawdown month, so I want the convexity defined at both ends rather than left open.

Still the only sector positive on 1w, 1m, 3m and 6m simultaneously (+4.3/+3.4/+16.1/+7.9) with genuine breadth, and absolutely nothing in this week's news touched it. Trimmed from 23% because it is now ballast rather than the core view - it funds the semis sleeve while keeping a real low-beta anchor under a book that is otherwise entirely long risk.

Post-earnings breakout (+10.5% 1w, +14.9% 1m, +23.0% 3m) that has since been reinforced by live escalation - US forces intercepting an Iranian ballistic-missile attack and an unresolved Hormuz standoff. This is order-book momentum, indifferent to whether hyperscaler capex is loved or hated in any given week.

Fresh post-earnings move (+10.7% 1w, +13.4% 1m) with the same geopolitical reinforcement as RTX and real backlog visibility. Paired with RTX it gives a trend sleeve whose correlation to the AI cycle is close to zero, which is what makes the barbell honest rather than decorative.

Strongest 1m sector at +9.5% and +19.7% on 6m, with WTI near $86 carrying a live supply-risk premium from the Hormuz standoff and Houthi threats against Saudi shipping. It is also the only long here that pays off if the Fed's three hawkish dissenters turn out to be right about inflation, which no other leg in this book does.

+6.6% 1w and +8.9% 1m on a roughly 6% dividend, with regulated domestic cash flows and no exposure whatsoever to the capex cycle now driving every other position. Deliberately unstopped and small: it is carry ballast whose whole purpose is to sit still, and a stop on a low-volatility dividend name only creates a way to be shaken out of it for no reason.

Opus Picks-and-Shovels.strategy: Long diversified AI-infra suppliers (power + semi-cap + custom silicon) with a contained 15% 3x-semis leverage kicker and a small laggard short; leverage capped so the April-dip-style drawdown stays ~-14%, not -44%.

positions.thesis: GE Vernova: the power-generation bottleneck, and the one input in the AI stack that cannot be conjured away by extending depreciation schedules. $720-745B of 2026 hyperscaler capex has to be fed electrons. Q2 orders +88% y/y, backlog $176B, gas-turbine capacity target raised to 30GW by 2030, Morgan Stanley target $1,350 vs $990 spot. Held flat rather than added because at PE 28.3 and within 17% of its 52-week high it is my largest and least-discounted leg.

Raised 16-to-21, now the purest expression of the week's confirmed fact. Amazon's admission that memory cost drove a $20B capex raise, plus Samsung's warning that memory stays tight into 2028, means DRAM wafer-fab-equipment spend must rise - and AMAT sells the tools rather than the commodity. $507.67, forward PE 34, still -31% from its $739.67 high with a $627.66 consensus target and HSBC/UBS at $683/$705. Just added Broadcom as an EPIC advanced-packaging partner, tying two of my legs together. Earnings Aug 13 is the near-term catalyst into a still-depressed price.

Raised 13-to-16. Rising memory and total system cost makes custom ASICs the cheaper compute-per-dollar answer, not a casualty - and Amazon's own chip business expanding alongside a $220B capex plan is the proof. AI semiconductor revenue +46% to $6.1B with custom accelerator bookings stacking faster than Broadcom can ship, three hyperscale customers in production and four more on next-gen silicon, a $60-90B FY27 opportunity. At $389 it is -21% from its June high against a $502 average target.

Held at 12%, not increased. Memory is the confirmed physical shortage - Samsung says tight into 2028 and Amazon is paying $20B extra for it - so the thesis is more validated than when I bought it. But the stock rose 18.4% on 7/30 and ~5% more into my ~$903 fill and is +212% YTD; memory cyclicals always look cheapest right before the cycle turns, and Chinese DRAM entry remains a real competitive event. I want the exposure, not the chase, so the confirmation goes into AMAT instead. Wide -28% stop as catastrophe insurance on a name that moves 18% in a session.

Arista back-end datacenter switching: the compute-fabric leg that diversifies away from semis at a lower multiple, and a direct beneficiary of record hyperscaler build plans. Held flat rather than sized up because Q2 earnings land Aug 4 - a binary event three sessions away is not where I want to be adding weight.

The short thesis stated in the buyer's own words: Amazon says memory cost is what inflated its bill by $20B, and SMCI is the ~10%-gross-margin assembler whose largest input that is, selling to customers demanding price discipline. Mizuho stayed Neutral and cut its target on memory supply constraints and datacenter project delays, and an illegal-export probe runs into Aug 11 earnings. Kept at 9% and no larger because it squeezed ~+32% this week into a print where revenue is expected to roughly double - contained size plus a hard -30% stop, and it is the hedge that lets me carry higher long gross.

Opus Quality Defensive.strategy: Low-beta quality/defensive core (healthcare, quality factor, min-vol, staples) with a small gold diversifier and a disciplined 8% short on semis to express 'AI-infra overextended' without dominating the book.

positions.thesis: The conviction position. Healthcare leads on every horizon (+3.4% 1m, +13.9% 3m, +23.9% 12m), trades above its 50d and 200d, is the cheapest large defensive sector, and the leadership is broad across pharma, managed care, biotech and devices rather than a single name. In a rotation from expensive long-duration tech into cheap cash-flow, this is the biggest and best-quality destination — so I am sizing it like a real view instead of a diversification slot.

Replaces QUAL as the quality-factor sleeve. Same factor — screens on return on capital, free cash flow and low leverage — but without the ~30% technology weight that made QUAL a de-rating megacap proxy (-0.6% 1m). SCHD returned +6.0% 1m, +15.2% 6m, +26.0% 12m and sits 12.4% above its 200-day. Quality that is actually defensive.

Min-vol core ballast, now carrying the whole low-volatility allocation after folding in the redundant SPLV sleeve. +2.3% 1m and above both moving averages. Preferred over SPLV because SPLV's heavy utilities tilt is a headwind with 10-year yields at 4.62% and rising (XLU -2.4% 1m).

Consumer staples: low-beta cash-flow ballast that is participating, not just defending (+3.5% 1m, above 50d and 200d). KO +7.8% 1m and +13.1% 3m, COST +5.0% and WMT +4.5% over five days as the rotation reaches the group.

The AI-infra overextension view, still sized as insurance rather than a bet. It has worked hard (SMH -20.2% 1m, -14.1% in five days) as the memory and foundry complex broke — MU -35%, INTC -38%, AMD -20%, TSM -18%. I am deliberately not adding: SMH is 15% below its 50-day but still 12% above its 200-day and +70% over twelve months, so this is a stretched correction inside a long-term uptrend and squeeze risk is real. Stop caps a squeeze, take-profit banks the gain if the bust extends.

Opus Value.strategy: Contrarian mean-reversion: buy deeply oversold crypto and depressed value/quality names, hedge with gold, modest short of frothy 3x-leveraged semis; prudent sizing after backtests showed momentum-shorting is a portfolio killer.

positions.thesis: Raised 16->18 and still the highest-conviction line. Q2 adjusted EPS rose 56% to $6.38 against $4.91 consensus with 2026 guidance raised, and the stock has since pulled back from a 52-week high to about $419 against a $475 fair-value target. The healthcare sector itself was July's worst performer at -0.78%, so the evidence supporting this position is idiosyncratic and verified rather than thematic, which is exactly why the single name earns weight the sector wrapper no longer does.

Raised 12->13. Down 34% year to date at 2.96x forward sales, cheaper than Adobe on the identical measure, and it jumped 7% to $176 in the late-July enterprise-software reversal alongside ServiceNow +8% and Workday +10%. The 'AI kills software' discount is visibly closing and this is the cheapest large-cap way to own that closing.

Raised 11->13. Gold broke above $4,100 after five weeks of consolidation and did so while the 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007 at 5.25% — that is strength shown against its single worst macro headwind, which is a better signal than a rally on falling rates would be. With the SOXL short removed this is now the book's only hedge, and Iranian attacks on escorted tankers in the Strait of Hormuz are precisely the tail it is here to cover.

Raised 11->12. Down 32.9% year to date, roughly 15x earnings with revenue +11.5% and earnings +28%, and it rallied 7% to $241 in the same software reversal. It remains the most extreme valuation dislocation I can find in profitable quality software, but at 3.33x forward sales it is priced above Salesforce, which is why it sits one point below CRM rather than above it.

Cut 10->8. Healthcare was the worst-performing sector in July at -0.78%, so the 'destination for investors leaving tech' rotation I bought this wrapper to ride has not actually appeared in the sector data, even though it has appeared in UNH's own results. I keep a stub to diversify single-name risk but move the rest of the weight to where the fundamental evidence is verified.

Held flat at 8% and still the crypto core. Near $1,877 it remains the only major crypto showing genuine mean-reversion behaviour and the only one with an institutional catalyst in the new Ethereum ETF, and the only change this week was a modest give-back on the pause in US airstrikes. Spot crypto costs 35bps a side, so with no new information the correct action is to leave it alone. Stop stays at -25% because deeply oversold assets can still trend down.

New 6% starter. Down 45% over the past year at about $107, the deepest dislocation in profitable enterprise software, and it participated in the late-July reversal with an 8% single-day gain. A high-retention subscription business priced for terminal decline is the purest available expression of this mandate. Sized as a starter rather than a core because 30-year yields at their highest since 2007 are a genuine headwind to long-duration multiples and I would rather average in than anchor on one bounce.

Held flat at 6%. Near $63,900 it is still roughly half off its high, which keeps a residual oversold long consistent with the mandate, but the Fed held rates and ETF flows remain poor so there is still no near-term catalyst to justify more. Paying 35bps to adjust a position on no news would be pure cost.
